title: Colour coding is a local choice: what applies in SA
audience: Cleaning staff and supervisors in SA healthcare facilities that use, or are considering, colour-coded equipment
learningOutcomes: State whether the SA standard requires colour coding
Explain what colour coding is meant to prevent
Apply a facility's colour scheme consistently

instruction.heading: Not required in SA
instruction.body: The SA standard does not require colour coding for cleaning items and tools in SA healthcare facilities. A facility can opt to adopt it voluntarily. Its purpose is to make sure that cloths, mop heads, buckets, aprons, gloves used in one area must never go into another, which lowers the chance of infection spreading between areas.

instruction.heading: The examples in the standard
instruction.body: The standard gives an example taken from schemes used in other jurisdictions. It assigns separate colours to bathrooms and toilets, to general areas, to food areas, and to isolation areas. These are examples only and do not form a required SA scheme. If a facility adopts a scheme, the colour must be easy to read and lasting on each item, and staff need training in how the system works.

instruction.heading: Other references that differ
instruction.body: Other reference documents use different colour assignments, including the Irish manual that is reviewed elsewhere in this set. Where another document conflicts with the SA standard, the SA standard governs in SA facilities. Do not adopt a colour chart from another document without the infection prevention team approving it for the facility.

procedure: Check the facility policy to find out whether colour coding is in use.
If it is, match each colour to its area using the facility's own chart, not memory.
Confirm that each colour marking is clear and permanent.
Keep each colour set with its own area and do not move items between colours.
Report any missing or faded colour markings to the supervisor.

workedExamples.situation: A facility uses a colour system. A cleaner takes a mop of the general-area colour into an isolation room because the isolation-colour mop is in the laundry.
workedExamples.reasoning: The mop must match the area it is used in. The cleaner gets the correct item from stock or reports the shortage so it can be fixed. Mixing colours defeats the purpose of the scheme.

equipmentAndPpe: Colour-marked cloths, mop heads, buckets, aprons, gloves

commonErrors.error: Using a colour chart from another facility
Moving a cloth from a bathroom set into a kitchen set
commonErrors.prevention: Store each colour set separately, with its area.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Colour coding is a cross-infection control tool. It is no substitute for hand hygiene or personal protective equipment.
Check any colour assignment against section 4.2.6 of the SA standard and the local policy.

qualityStandard: The learner states that the SA standard leaves colour coding optional
The learner matches a sample item to its area on the facility chart
documentationEvidence: Facility colour chart signed off by the infection prevention team, if the scheme is in use
summary: The SA standard does not require colour coding
Colour coding stops materials for one area being used in another
Use the facility's chart; other documents do not override the SA standard

knowledgeChecks.question: Does the SA standard require colour coding in healthcare facilities?
options: Yes, in every facility and in every ward and clinic
No, it is optional and a facility may adopt it voluntarily
Yes, but only for isolation rooms and only in the theatre

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the main purpose of colour coding?
options: To make the storeroom look organised for the manager's visit
To keep cleaning materials for one area from being used in another
To replace hand hygiene and to save the cost of gloves

knowledgeChecks.question: A cleaner picks up a mop of the wrong colour for the area. What should happen?
options: Use it once and return it later to the same room
Replace it with the correct colour or report the shortage
Wash it and use it in any area once it is dry again
